//: Typecheck-only view of e2e/, covering what the other two configs cannot.
`tsconfig.app.json` includes `src` and `tsconfig.node.json` includes exactly
one file, `vite.config.ts`. Measured with `--listFiles`: the app program is
1 960 files, 1 313 of them under `src/`, and ZERO under `e2e/`. So 58 spec
and helper files, four `playwright*.config.ts` and `vitest.config.ts` were
compiled by nothing and checked by nothing — Playwright transpiles without
typechecking, exactly as vitest does, so a `@ts-expect-error` in a spec was
decoration too.
This is `server/tsconfig.check.json`'s remedy applied to the directory it
does not reach, and it is the same hole: that config exists because
`qa/eviction-check.mts` called a five-parameter function with four arguments
and reported FAIL on every run for an unknown period.
WHAT THE FIRST RUN FOUND, 292 errors:
- 275 were the cascade from seven spec files each declaring their own
`window.__scene3d`, five their own `__canvasEngine`, two their own
`__modelStore`, and four writing out `SceneStats` by hand — two of those
four missing the GPU leak-accounting fields. Each file typechecked ALONE
because its own version of the truth was the only one in scope. One
declared `resetCamera()`, which the probe does not install at all.
- 17 were real type errors in five files, found by nothing until now.
The declarations are now `e2e/support/probes.d.ts`, and the probe's shape
comes from `src/canvas3d/scene3dProbe.ts`, which `Scene3D.mount()` checks its
literal against with `satisfies`.
WHY A SEPARATE CONFIG — and the first version of this note gave two
reasons that a review lens measured false, so both are corrected here
rather than quietly replaced.
It said e2e needs `types: [node]` which the app program 'must not have'.
BOTH halves of that are false, and each was measured by a different lens.
App's own options over `include: [src]` plus `types: [node]` compiles with
ZERO errors — keeping `node:fs` unreachable from browser code is a fine
POLICY, not a compile constraint. And `node` in the array below is INERT:
with it removed the gate stays green, because `@types/node` reaches this
program transitively through `@playwright/test`. Four mutants:
types entry removed entirely  -> green (inherits app's [vite/client])
[vite/client]  (node dropped) -> green   <- node is doing nothing
[node] (vite/client dropped)  -> 32 errors, TS2882 + TS2339
[]                            -> 32 errors
So `vite/client` is what is load-bearing here, and `node` is KEPT anyway,
deliberately: an ambient type arriving through someone else's dependency is
the same fragility as the undeclared `cbor-x` this branch just fixed one
package over. Declaring it says what this program needs and survives
@playwright/test dropping it. What is not acceptable is a comment claiming
it is the mechanism when it is not — the rule that a comment asserting a mechanism must be true, and the THIRD
invented mechanism found on this branch, each one in the commit that adds a
detector for the neighbouring class.
And it argued against widening `tsconfig.app.json`'s `include` — which is
not the alternative anyone would propose. The root `tsconfig.json` is
already a solution file with a `references` array, and app is `noEmit`, so
adding `{ path: ./tsconfig.e2e.json }` makes `tsc -b` cover e2e and deletes
three wires (this npm script, the ci.yml step, the ci-local.mjs line). That
option was never evaluated. It works: the reference regenerates this
config's tsbuildinfo, which the plain `tsc -b` does not.
The real reason to stay split, stated properly: `tsc -b` is the first half
of `npm run build`, the command that produces the DEPLOYABLE. A reference
makes a type error in a Playwright spec fail the release build. CI already
runs lint, build and `typecheck:e2e` in one job, so coverage is identical
either way — the only question is whether shipping should be gated on test
code, and here it should not.
NOTE what this makes `server/tsconfig.check.json` as a precedent: WEAKER
than it looks. The server's split is FORCED (`tsconfig.json` emits, with
`rootDir: ./src`, and server has no solution file); this one is a choice.
Copying the shape past its own precondition is the mistake to avoid —
'a rule is a claim about a condition;
check the condition, not the shape'.
Run: npm run typecheck:e2e   (wired into `node scripts/ci-local.mjs --static`)
